Peter,
At Jon’s rally earlier this month, he called out the corruption — on both sides of the aisle — that drives American politics.
> _**“The Mar-a-Lago mafia has taken American corruption to spectacular new heights, but corruption in America runs a lot deeper than Donald Trump.** Because how does American politics really work?_
> _It's coin-operated. Money goes in, favors come out. It's been running on secret money, corporate money, billionaire money. Both sides._
> Citizens United _was the worst court decision in modern American history._
> _It's why members of Congress don't listen to the people; they listen to their donors.”_
**But it doesn’t have to be this way.**
Everywhere our campaign goes, all across Georgia, people are screaming out for change and an end to the corruption and greed that seem to drive our politics.
Peter, the fight to save our Republic is more important now than maybe ever before.
If we stand together, we can send a resounding message to MAGA, escape this moral tailspin, and recommit ourselves to the values that have made this country great.
**But none of that is possible without victory this November, and Jon needs you in his corner.**
[**Please, make your first contribution to Jon’s reelection campaign today.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-april26.1MDdBw&refcode=em260427-1-f-b&t=2&akid=2190%2E5691347%2E0wL_SZ)
In 2020, the pundits said flipping a Republican Senate seat in Georgia couldn’t be done. But we built one of the strongest voter mobilization programs in Senate campaign history — and _we won_. That victory won the Senate majority.
Now we must win again. And we _will win again._
Just like last time, Jon can’t do it alone.
So we are humbly asking:

I’ve spent my life fixing things that are broken.
On the factory floor.
In the Navy.
In the National Guard.
And right now, there’s nothing more broken than the United States Senate.
Washington isn’t working for people like us anymore. It’s working for billionaires, lobbyists, and corporations that write the rules for themselves — and leave the rest of us footing the bill.
I’m Dan Osborn, and I’m running for Senate to fix Washington. Please, chip in $10, $25, or whatever you can right now to help me → [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
DONATE TODAY TO DEFEAT MAGA EXTREMISM! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
I’m not a career politician. I’m an industrial mechanic from Omaha, a former union leader who took on Kellogg’s to protect my coworkers’ wages and benefits, and a guy who knows what it means to work 80-hour weeks just to keep a middle-class life together.
And I’m running as an independent because I don’t owe either party a damn thing.
I owe you.
I’ll fight to cut taxes for working families, protect Social Security, stand up for family farms, and finally pass Right to Repair so corporations stop ripping people off just to fix what they own.
But I can’t do this alone. The same billionaires who broke Washington are going to spend whatever it takes to keep it that way.
So I’m asking: Will you chip in $10, $25, or anything you can right now to help us build a campaign that answers to working people — not the powerful? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-osborn]
Let's fix this.
—Dan Osborn

body:

Friend,

Here in New Jersey and across the country, people are struggling to make ends meet, and MAGA is only making things worse.

They just voted to slash healthcare funding, including cuts to Medicaid, which hurts families across our district and puts hospitals at risk of closing.

This is exactly the problem with MAGA: they're reckless, inconsiderate, and doing nothing to make life easier for everyday people.

It's never been more important to put a stop to their agenda. That's why we're working to re-elect Nellie and get one step closer to taking back the House in November.

This bill is part of a comprehensive legislative response I co-led in the wake of the tragic 2025 mid-air collision at DCA. ### _Celebrate Journalism. Empower Future Storytellers._

Greetings,

Last Saturday our fourth Annual Brown and Bougie Brunch was a success in large part because of your support. Thank you for attending and celebrating our Jovita Idar Awardees, Washington Post's, Arelis R. Hernández and independent journalist, Nick Valencia. This year, we also launched the Independent Media Vanguard Award, presented to Rafael Collazo, Executive Director for Unidos US Action Fund.

Peter,

**April is Fair Housing Month - and that means something simple: everyone should be able to live in and afford the places they call home.**

But right now, that’s not the reality for far too many. America is in the middle of a housing crisis - one that has been decades in the making, and families are paying the price.

That’s why I’ve spent years in California reforming the rules that made it so difficult and expensive to build housing - unlocking tens of thousands of homes, including over 3,000 in San Francisco.

[**Now I’m running for Congress to take that fight nationwide - and I’m asking for your support.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130274363/617206987/-2023653193?amount=10&refcode=SW_EM_FR_180DO_260427_1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MDY5OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZjYzMGZhOS03MDQyLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=oarsCPqh9JADXu-bleZwlqV0PaNU7zPFauUUJxrP9_g=)

_Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona_
---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

clean_body: This is the part most people don’t see | | | | | Peter, I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground. Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible. Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them. They're already claimed. And we don't have extras. By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in. Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it. That's where things stand right now. We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment. And I don't say that lightly. Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down. The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great. And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing. Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back. We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there. And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet. That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens. And it's not isolated growth anymore. We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America. That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation... And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak. So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build. Our newest candidate is unapologetically pro-peace and pro-Palestine.
#
Peter,
Pennsylvania’s 3rd district is our next big primary fight, and it’s shaping up to be a battle between a pro-Palestine, anti-war candidate and the pro-Israel lobby.
Our candidate, State Rep. Chris Rabb, is unapologetically opposed to AIPAC and calls what Israel is doing in Gaza what it is: _genocide._
Meanwhile, **one of his biggest opponents in this open primary has already received $1.4 million from one of AIPAC’s old shell PACs,** 314 Action Fund. It comes as no surprise that she avoids calling Israel’s actions genocide.
When Chris was asked about AIPAC at a recent candidate forum, his response was simple: **“F-ck AIPAC.”**
After applause broke out, he went on to say, “They are a racist organization and I will not meet with them.”
This is the bluest congressional district in the country, so there’s no excuse to elect yet another pro-Israel establishment Democrat — we need a progressive fighter for peace and the working-class, and that’s Chris.

body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240813%2E444211%2E5HHO1A)
Part of what makes our work so effective, and the thing I love most about what we do, is the time we spend meeting and talking with young Texans across the state.
There’s this line from Rush: “All this machinery making modern music can still be open-hearted. Not so coldly charted, it's really just a question of your honesty.”
So much of modern politics is soul crushing. Formulaic TV ads, consultant-driven talking points, canned social media provocation... and everything else that money can buy and technology can produce.
But there’s a way to bypass all that and get back to the soul of self-government. It just requires spending time with people and listening to what they have to say.
Our volunteers (and I’m one of them) meet people where they are, on college campuses, at concerts, in clubs, outside of churches and have open, honest conversations with them about what’s happening in our country and what it will take to make it better.
That’s the open-hearted approach that builds trust and ensures that we can register new voters, confirm registrations for existing ones and — in all cases — personally stay in touch to ensure that they vote.
That last part is key. When I say we personally stay in touch, that means the volunteer who met that young student on campus is the one to text or call them to share important voting information and to encourage them to vote until their ballot is cast.
We took young voter turnout from 37% to 79% in 2024 by taking this open-hearted approach, by treating people as humans instead of numbers and by doing the work that works.
[**Please support this unique, independent and honest connection that we’re making all across Texas by donating what you can today.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260427.jdRQn3&refcode=ema20260427-240813&t=3&akid=240813%2E444211%2E5HHO1A)
Thank you,
Beto

> > It's not often that Supreme Court Justice's take the stage to talk about American politics, however, it's even more rare when they take to the stage and point the fingers at America's villains. On Wednesday, April 15th, 2026, the Honorable Justice Clarence Thomas did exactly that while speaking at the University of Texas in Austin; doing so on the heels of the 250thanniversary of the Declaration of Independence.
>
> Justice Thomas delivered a rare and scathing rebuke of modern-day progressivism, and the ideological force he regards as an "existential threat to the very foundation upon which America was built." He didn't mince words; he lamented how the core values cherished by the founding fathers have "fallen out of favor," warning that the nation is careening toward intellectual and moral ruin if younger generations fail to reclaim our foundational principles.
>> [Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6729589&post_id=195660523&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk1NjYwNTIzLCJpYXQiOjE3NzczMjAyNjgsImV4cCI6MTc3OTkxMjI2OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTY3Mjk1ODkiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.3pSz-EN3j4Jl40n0-3FPQWjfCADf0uHLfE3XCErhHsY)
>> This wasn't a nostalgic call for patriotism; it was a blunt indictment of the progressive agenda that has stealthily redefined American society in the last two decades. The consequences from the radical ideology have been profound and far from benign. Progressivism under the guise of equity and social justice promotes policies that almost always reward identity over achievement.
>
> This isn't about uplifting the disadvantaged; it's about redistributing success based on group identity and victimhood. This has created a culture that actively disincentivizes personal accountability and excellence, while replacing ambition with grievance. When you dictate how people should think rather than encourage independent thought, you kill initiative and innovation; the two engines that have powered America's rise to glory.
>
> Justice Thomas nailed it when he said, "If we don't stand up and take ownership of our country, and take responsibility for it, we are slowly letting others control how we think and what we think." He understands that the poison of progressivism has seeped into education, the media, and government institutions; areas once devoted to fostering critical thinking and civic pride, have now been transformed into echo chambers of ideological conformity.
>
>
> Progressivism demands unquestioning acceptance of its worldly view, while punishing dissent and labeling it as hate or ignorance. It preys on the conscience of good people, turning them into blind useful idiots. Its embrace of identity politics and intersectionality fractures national unity by pitting groups against one another. Instead of promoting a shared identity as Americans, it focuses on dividing citizens into classes of oppressors and oppressed.
>> | [](https://substack.com/redirect/143608e0-1d7a-457f-9226-296d995adcca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
>> ---|---|---
>> This brand of divisive tribalism undermines social cohesion and breeds resentment within the population, making it easier for political opportunists to manipulate public sentiment and weaken constitutional governance. We see this play out in blue cities across the country where progressive leadership has the majority. Recent elections in New York and Seattle's mayoral races accentuate this very point.
>
> Justice Thomas's speech also highlighted what he called a "generational crisis." He spoke how young Americans are being educated in an environment that increasingly rejects the principles of free inquiry and robust debate. Instead of encouraging students to grapple with complex ideas from independent judgments, colleges push ideological conformity masked as diversity and inclusion.
>
> In doing so, this distorts history, censors opposing viewpoints, and conditions America's youth to accept a world where authority dictates the truth, rather than evidence or reason. The long-term consequence is a citizenry that is ill-prepared to defend liberty or even comprehend its true value.
>
> Justice's Thomas's blistering critique shines a harsh light on these realities, holding progressivism accountable for its dangerous trajectory. He calls on America to awaken from the complacency slumber that has allowed these currents to take hold unchallenged. He makes the choice abundantly clear; either revive commitment to America's founding ideals or surrender to a future where the nations identity is completely fragmented, unrecognizable, and hollowed out.
>
> The real danger here isn't some external enemy but the internal rot that corrodes civic virtue and national coherence from within. Justice Thomas rightfully reminds us that safeguarding liberty requires vigilance, courage and, above all, reclaiming ownership of our country, intellectually, morally, and politically. He also reminds us that the framework for repair already exists within our Declaration of Independence. It simply requires reading the first few paragraphs from time to time.
>
> Editorial comments expressed in this column are the sole opinion of the writer.

Instead of promoting a shared identity as Americans, it focuses on dividing citizens into classes of oppressors and oppressed. > | | > ---|---|--- > This brand of divisive tribalism undermines social cohesion and breeds resentment within the population, making it easier for political opportunists to manipulate public sentiment and weaken constitutional governance. We see this play out in blue cities across the country where progressive leadership has the majority. Recent elections in New York and Seattle's mayoral races accentuate this very point. Justice Thomas's speech also highlighted what he called a "generational crisis." He spoke how young Americans are being educated in an environment that increasingly rejects the principles of free inquiry and robust debate. Instead of encouraging students to grapple with complex ideas from independent judgments, colleges push ideological conformity masked as diversity and inclusion. In doing so, this distorts history, censors opposing viewpoints, and conditions America's youth to accept a world where authority dictates the truth, rather than evidence or reason. The long-term consequence is a citizenry that is ill-prepared to defend liberty or even comprehend its true value. Justice's Thomas's blistering critique shines a harsh light on these realities, holding progressivism accountable for its dangerous trajectory. He calls on America to awaken from the complacency slumber that has allowed these currents to take hold unchallenged. He makes the choice abundantly clear; either revive commitment to America's founding ideals or surrender to a future where the nations identity is completely fragmented, unrecognizable, and hollowed out. The real danger here isn't some external enemy but the internal rot that corrodes civic virtue and national coherence from within. Justice Thomas rightfully reminds us that safeguarding liberty requires vigilance, courage and, above all, reclaiming ownership of our country, intellectually, morally, and politically. He also reminds us that the framework for repair already exists within our Declaration of Independence. It simply requires reading the first few paragraphs from time to time. Chris

# CA Police Chiefs Association Endorses Magsig for Senate
---
|
---
| | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** April 27th, 2026Contact: nathan@nathanmagsig.com
---
| | | | | | **(Clovis, CA)** \- Today, Nathan Magsig announced the endorsement of the California Police Chiefs Association for his campaign for State Senate.
Magsig expressed his appreciation for the endorsement, stating:
_“It’s a tremendous honor to earn the support of police chiefs from across California who are on the front lines of keeping our communities safe. Throughout my time in local government, I’ve worked closely with law enforcement to prioritize public safety, support strong partnerships, and ensure our officers have the tools and backing they need. In the State Senate, I will continue to stand up for policies that protect our communities and support those who serve.”_
The endorsement from the California Police Chiefs Association adds to Magsig’s growing coalition of public safety support, reinforcing his commitment to law and order and highlighting his record of working alongside law enforcement leaders to deliver results.
View the full list of endorsements [HERE](https://nathanmagsig.us8.list-manage.com/track/click?u=566959e132b9980afc6311201&id=929279b754&e=6cdbd718cb)

Nathan Magsig is a current Fresno County Supervisor, former Mayor of Clovis, and is running for the 12th Senate District. His family, wife Julie and their three children, reside in Clovis, CA.

body:
I’ll get straight to the point because I value your time:

We’re lagging $13,234 behind our April fundraising goal that we _need_ to hit in order to power our efforts to flip the Senate.

Before I go any farther, I have to ask: [**_Can you please chip in whatever makes sense for you right now, so we can close our fundraising gap?_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130276922/617215489/1146729020?amount=5&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.04.27_Slow-Month-RH_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiOTcxOWE3YS03NzQyLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=hgELsvhzUseQfBUVZqL_qn-xTjqdX8Gg4vVy2qBRTNk=)

If things don’t turn around quickly, we may not have the resources we need to support key battleground Senate races.

Hey Peter, it's Tim.
In a moment, I’m going to ask if you’ll [**become a founding donor to help us get Small Town PAC off the ground.**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260427.Ednl_3&amount=5&refcode=em20260427-542&t=1&akid=542%2E34582%2EdPSQ44) Before I do, I hope you’ll let me explain how your contribution will make a difference.
It’s officially been one week since I launched Small Town PAC, and we’re already approaching our first fundraising deadline at midnight on Thursday, April 30. To kick this organization off on a strong note, **I’ve set a goal of raising $100,000 before the month ends.**
Small Town PAC is all about laying the foundation for recruiting and training regular, working-class people in small towns to run for office and give their communities the representation they deserve at every level of government.
Billionaires, venture capitalists, and tech bros are spending more money than ever before in history to buy our elections. They’re lining up to support spineless Republicans like J.D. Vance, who are willing to sell out their communities back home, all to funnel more wealth into the hands of the already rich and powerful.
_It’s not right._ That’s why it’s time for small towns to take their power back and for Democrats to expand the map through fresh, bold leadership.
The size and speed of the impact we make will depend directly on how much we raise from emails like this one: the more grassroots resources we build, the more states and races we can get involved in, and the faster we grow, the sooner we can get to work.
Right now, **our average donation is just $24.09, and we’re about $27,500 away from hitting our launch goal.** With folks like you pitching in whatever you can spare, I know we can get there in the next three days.
[**So what do you say? Can I count on you to chip in $5 or more today?**](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260427.Ednl_3&amount=5&refcode=em20260427-542&t=2&akid=542%2E34582%2EdPSQ44)

Tim

#### I need your immediate attention: Trump and his MAGA Republicans are doing everything in their power to undercut my campaign. So, we need to fight back, but as of right now, we're falling 2,097 contributions short of where we need to be. That's why I'm reaching out to my top grassroots supporters and asking for $10.
#### If I can close this fundraising gap, I know we can set the record straight, win this crucial primary, and send a fighter to Congress who will stand up to Trump's MAGA agenda. **[So please, can I count on you to stand with my campaign for Maryland's 5th District by chipping in $10 before midnight? >>](https://substack.com/redirect/d881c568-c7a4-4661-b207-2f9ba878d6b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Here's what I need you to know:
1. I defended the Capitol on January 6th while Donald Trump did NOTHING for hours as the Capitol Police force were harassed, attacked, beaten, and more by his supporters.
2. I'm running in a HIGHLY COMPETITIVE race that could determine the House Majority.
3. If I can win this crucial seat, I'll be able to hold Trump and his MAGA enablers accountable in Congress and fight for our democracy.
4. I'm not a self-funded millionaire. I rely solely on the support of grassroots Democrats like you to fund our critical campaign.
5. So, my team and I set an ambitious $500,000 end-of-month goal to show Trump we're NOT afraid and will NOT back down from this fight.

#### **[But I have to be blunt with you: We can't afford to waste a single second. Trump will stop at nothing to destroy our grassroots campaign. Please, can you dig deep and rush $10 before midnight to help me take back our House Majority and fight for our Democracy?](https://substack.com/redirect/d881c568-c7a4-4661-b207-2f9ba878d6b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Thank you,

Harry Dunn

body:

I was just in Philomath this weekend, sitting in a small town hall with neighbors asking honest questions about something that should never be controversial: how they can trust that their vote will be counted.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
Here’s what I told them — and what I need you to hear too.
Oregon’s elections are secure, accurate, and built to work for real life. Vote-by-mail works. Drop boxes work. And people across our state rely on both to make their voices heard.
But right now, those systems are under pressure from every direction.
Just this week, Oregon joined other states in court to block yet another unconstitutional attempt to interfere with how Americans vote. We’ve already beat these attacks before — and we intend to do it again.
But defending our elections isn’t just happening in courtrooms. It’s happening in every county, every clerk’s office, and every community where voters are deciding how to return their ballots.
This work takes vigilance. It takes resources. And it takes a public willing to stand up for a simple idea: that democracy belongs to the people who live here—not to politicians trying to rewrite the rules from the top down.
We’re going to keep strengthening our elections. And we’re going to keep making sure every eligible Oregonian can cast a ballot safely and confidently.
If you’re with me in this fight to protect voting rights in Oregon, I’m asking you to pitch in today. Your support helps us communicate directly with Oregonians and defend vote-by-mail, secure our elections, and push back against dangerous attempts to make it harder for people to vote. Just this week, Oregon joined other states in court to block yet another unconstitutional attempt to interfere with how Americans vote. We’ve already beat these attacks before — and we intend to do it again. But defending our elections isn’t just happening in courtrooms. It’s happening in every county, every clerk’s office, and every community where voters are deciding how to return their ballots. This work takes vigilance. It takes resources. And it takes a public willing to stand up for a simple idea: that democracy belongs to the people who live here—not to politicians trying to rewrite the rules from the top down. We’re going to keep strengthening our elections. And we’re going to keep making sure every eligible Oregonian can cast a ballot safely and confidently. If you’re with me in this fight to protect voting rights in Oregon, I’m asking you to pitch in today. Your support helps us communicate directly with Oregonians and defend vote-by-mail, secure our elections, and push back against dangerous attempts to make it harder for people to vote. body:
Over the past few months, I’ve spent a lot of time listening, reflecting,
and thinking about what this moment demands of us.

What I keep coming back to is this: people are looking for leadership that
shows up, tells the truth, and is willing to fight for what matters. I’ve
run in tough places. I’ve won in tough places. And I still believe the
path forward is the same as it’s always been: go where the fight is, say
what you believe, and make the case everywhere.

That’s why I’m launching Small Town PAC.

I believe small towns still matter. The people in them still matter. And
if Democrats want to build a stronger party, we’ve got to be willing to
show up, listen, organize, and compete in more places. We can’t keep
writing off communities and expect to start winning them back.

Small Town PAC is about helping put power back in the hands of our
neighbors and building a party that takes these places seriously again.
It’s about expanding the map, supporting leaders who actually understand
these communities, and fighting for the schools, jobs, and future small
towns deserve.

Dear Patriot, They're trying to put an innocent cop in prison for **life**. Why? For defending himself against a fleeing suspect who dragged him with a car. I've been in law enforcement for decades. I've seen the system abused. But what is happening to Officer James Brennand of San Antonio, Texas makes my blood boil, and it should make yours boil too. On October 2nd, 2022, Officer James Brennand — a decorated Army veteran who swore an oath to protect his community — spotted a car he suspected was stolen outside a McDonald's in San Antonio. He called for backup. He approached the vehicle. He ordered the driver to step out. The driver's response? He threw the car into reverse and used it as a weapon. | [Defend Officer Brennand →](http://links.g4yamerica.com/u/click?_t=cc7dda5c2cc64061900678c88bd3a18a&_m=69ceb3c6ddfa4778b1449f7c5ca7114a&_e=wlPSr-V8OXi66gG3POKdDv1xEi-voCvNlkJ8w7mHi2_-5d6009BJSgrYnQzIW3UIq6XgkeEcwebefHc5AqesA7blHH6Z4svPBTCCItdNzTY9lpUt9FDykRSbQNMOGQODmEME7rSOr_p85gO1VI_hXEzLLTm6JTtpZrrrJgxNRCjUV1huPFCB327bDoVWji9Ob88l7YJdGvtMkvnJ32oM_57KFguGp-IF6mBfpY_f1mjhNWo45-9g6CfbS3R5MB7thD1sfc1I7Qt495rB3IqqPorfFw5Q26IdzFOeiyg4RtFrSs8xsiEUI9Dad57Gqg0TPjlqJBDF40a9hZ8kn60fv_BrBbZph5LsocLELXcgUDeDEX49BAU9FBI5JzXO0BaO1Voi-JVfsiR3C1_5LEhY7zhSpyKulhn3TWTrcAKKWhgvEN48lUiAJrYydKaUq8m8)
---
The car door slammed into Brennand. He was dragged. In that split second — outnumbered, without backup, in genuine danger — James did what every officer is trained to do. **He protected himself.**
The driver survived. The passenger was unharmed. And since that night, the driver has racked up four more arrests. **Four.**
While the man who attacked James faces no meaningful consequences, Officer Brennand has been stripped of his badge, his paycheck, and his future. A politically hungry District Attorney — more interested in headlines than justice — charged James with aggravated assault and deadly conduct. If convicted: **five years to life.**
Let that sink in. A man who served his country in the Army, who volunteered to protect the streets of San Antonio, who was dragged by a car in the line of duty — could die in prison.

clean_body: | Dear Patriot, They're trying to put an innocent cop in prison for life. Why? For defending himself against a fleeing suspect who dragged him with a car. I've been in law enforcement for decades. I've seen the system abused. But what is happening to Officer James Brennand of San Antonio, Texas makes my blood boil, and it should make yours boil too. On October 2nd, 2022, Officer James Brennand — a decorated Army veteran who swore an oath to protect his community — spotted a car he suspected was stolen outside a McDonald's in San Antonio. He called for backup. He approached the vehicle. He ordered the driver to step out. The driver's response? He threw the car into reverse and used it as a weapon. | The car door slammed into Brennand. He was dragged. In that split second — outnumbered, without backup, in genuine danger — James did what every officer is trained to do. He protected himself. The driver survived. The passenger was unharmed. And since that night, the driver has racked up four more arrests. Four. While the man who attacked James faces no meaningful consequences, Officer Brennand has been stripped of his badge, his paycheck, and his future. A politically hungry District Attorney — more interested in headlines than justice — charged James with aggravated assault and deadly conduct. If convicted: five years to life. Let that sink in. A man who served his country in the Army, who volunteered to protect the streets of San Antonio, who was dragged by a car in the line of duty — could die in prison. James and his son — a family now fighting for survival while awaiting trial. The National Center for Police Defense is in this fight with James — funding his legal defense and supporting his family while this nightmare drags on toward trial. name: David Hogg
subject: “No experience, no leadership, no accountability”
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
While Stephen Lynch was talking down to young voters and leaders, Patrick Roath was showing them what real progressive leadership looks like.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260427-1&t=1&akid=3412%2E587540%2ESXlAGz)
Peter,
**_“Nowadays, kids get up in the morning, and they think they see a member of Congress in the mirror -- no experience, no leadership, no accountability.” _**
That dig was meant for Leaders We Deserve-endorsed candidate **Patrick Roath** , a 39 year old lawyer and father. And it came from Stephen Lynch, the incumbent he’s challenging in Massachusetts.
Condescending? Out of touch? Exactly what’s wrong with the Democratic Party? Check, check, check. ✅
Because here’s the thing. Stephen meant that as an insult, but **young people _should_ wake up everyday and see themselves reflected in members of Congress**. They _should_ feel empowered to not only participate in our democracy, but to lead it with their bold, fresh perspectives. That’s the entire point we’ve been making at Leaders We Deserve.
**[If that’s the kind of Democratic Party you believe in, pitch in $5 right now to help Leaders We Deserve keep building that future.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260427_1_roath.BzBUIN&refcode=em20260427-3412&amount=5&t=2&akid=3412%2E587540%2ESXlAGz)**
Stephen has been in Congress for almost 25 years. And throughout his tenure, he’s repeatedly failed young voters and working class families.
He voted against the Affordable Care Act -- and he’s the last Democrat left in Congress to have done so. He backed the Laken Riley Act that helped expand the Trump administration’s mass deportation campaign. And just a couple months ago, he mocked frustrated constituents when they called him out for his lukewarm resistance against Trump, telling them, “if you don’t like it, run for Congress.”
While Stephen was talking down to voters and the next generation of Democratic leaders, **Patrick and I were walking the Freedom Trail with several dozen college students, showing them that democracy belongs to them, and there are candidates who actually want them in the room.**
That’s who Patrick is. Not only does he have the **experience** , **leadership** , and **accountability** to make him a force in Congress, he also is a leader who **listens** , **inspires** , and **treats young voters like they matter**. That’s what it looks like to build a Democratic Party that people actually want to be a part of.
Voters are sick and tired of entitled politicians who act like they’re untouchable, especially in safe seats like this one. They’re ready for fearless progressive fighters like Patrick who are worthy of their trust and will offer them a bolder vision.
**[Will you pitch in $5 to help Leaders We Deserve continue backing candidates like Patrick who will meet this moment without flinching, and fight for working people instead of their own political survival?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260427_1_roath.BzBUIN&refcode=em20260427-3412&amount=5&t=3&akid=3412%2E587540%2ESXlAGz)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260427_1_roath.BzBUIN&amount=5&refcode=em20260427-3412&t=22&akid=3412%2E587540%2ESXlAGz)**
Thank you,
David Hogg

It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 _ _ and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. clean_body: This Memorial Day begins America’s 250th – join me| | | Patriot, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Patriot, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Patriot, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. The 2026 National Memorial Day Parade is a once-in-a-lifetime moment where we need to do all we can to honor our country and our veterans. Bigger crowds. More veterans. More young people learning what courage, service, and sacrifice really mean. Historically, AVC has been able to do this at a fraction of what other major public events cost to put on each year. In fact, the entire parade costs about as much as just THREE balloons in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade or TWO floats in the Rose Bowl Parade! That means that every dollar that's contributed by a generous American like you makes a difference for this important event. But I want to reiterate that American Veterans Center does not take ANY federal funding for this event. It is funded entirely by private citizens like you who want to honor those who have sacrificed so much for our country. | | Your support of the American Veterans Center not only helps the parade, but also supports great programs like: Record hundreds of oral histories of veterans from World War II to today before we lose these stories forever. Hold our annual American Veterans Conference, which allows young cadets a chance to hear first-hand from veterans from WWII, Korea, Vietnam, and our modern wars. Produce veteran-focused T.V. documentaries and specials that remind Americans the price of our freedom. But of course, the National Memorial Day Parade is AVC's flagship event honoring America's veterans. And this year's parade will be the largest in their history of hosting the parade. If you've been looking for an opportunity to give back to those who have given so much for our freedom, this is one of the best possible ways you could do it. And for a special group of veterans, this might be one of the last chances we get. You see, with each year that goes by, we lose more and more of our World War II veterans, and for the few we have remaining, traveling to Washington, D.C., for the parade is difficult. | | | | | WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade. This year is a rare moment when living witnesses to World War II and America 's 250**th birthday overlap. And no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. - On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more. Patriot, thank you for your support of America 's heroes. Sincerely, Gary Sinise Honarary Grand MarshalNational Memorial Day Parade P.S. And for the Greatest Generation in particular, this may be the last time they're able to join us at this year's National Memorial Day Parade. There's no better send-off we can give them than to make sure they're present to honor their fallen brethren during America's 250th birthday. I never thought that I would run for office when I was a little girl — let alone become the first woman governor of New York.
When I was born, my parents had just moved out of a trailer and into a small apartment in Woodlawn, New York.
My dad worked long shifts at the steel mill. I watched my mother — who raised six kids — stretch every dollar by buying used clothes and serving fried spam sandwiches for dinner.
Witnessing the struggles and pain of those left behind inspired me to run for office, to be a voice for communities that had fallen on hard times, because I had lived that experience.

Peter, MAGA Mayes Middleton is confused. I’m not.

**Middleton thinks that the Texas AG should “use every resource and tool to advance [President Trump’s] conservative agenda.”**

That’s not the job, Mayes. The Texas AG is not a presidential appointee or employee or servant or lackey. The job of an attorney general is not and has never been to advance any president’s agenda.

**Middleton also believes the “number one” goal of this office is to “defeat the Left.”**
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130280238/617226540/-181195618?amount=15&refcode=NJ_EM_FR_042726_B1_MAGAMayesRS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTQyOSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNzRlM2Q0Yy04MzQyLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pGNVvo50OzNPz6o3sF1bNi97D0ZgVk2g4-MfvnHgyIk=)
The job of the Attorney General is not to defeat the Left or impose a far right radical agenda, or anybody’s agenda.

It is:
→ to root out corruption.
→ to protect individual rights.
→ to block federal overreach.
→ to assist in public safety.
→ to ensure fair and honest markets.
→ to protect consumers from predatory business practices.
→ to uphold the rule of law in the private sector and in the public sector.
→ to act as a check on the abuse of power.

**Middleton doesn’t understand the job. I do.**

As your Attorney General, I will serve as a constitutional check on the abuse of power, uphold the law, protect your rights, and serve the people of Texas.

**This office can be powerfully good under the right leadership.**

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Now that it’s public, I’ve had the chance to read through it carefully.

Campaign finance reports are one of the few places you can see, in plain text, who a candidate is actually accountable to.

**Here’s how whose funding him affects you:**

●**Start with your mortgage and your rent:** The National Association of Realtors PAC, The American Bankers Association, and America's Credit Unions PAC.

●**Look at your electric bill and what you pay at the pump:** Koch PAC – the political operation of one of the largest oil, gas, and chemical companies in the country, and The Energy Marketers of America.

●**Then look at what you pay for healthcare:** The American College of Radiology PAC, The American Association of Orthopedic Surgeons, United Health Services, and The American Health Care Association.

None of that is illegal or even unusual for a Republican running for Congress. However, it really speaks to who he’s already about to owe favors to before he’s even sworn into office.

My report is going to look different because we're building this campaign a different way. Our donors are teachers in Athens, retirees in Jefferson, nurses in Walton County, and small business owners in Madison. The audacity of evil has no bounds, Patriot. | "" This morning, I was in a Miami courtroom fighting to get my constitutional rights restored. We had to bring in attorneys pro hac vice from multiple jurisdictions -- lawyers who don't normally practice in this court, specially admitted just to defend me. That costs a small fortune. But here's what happened: Judge Marie E. Mato overturned the firearms prohibition. Her words from the bench: "Mr. O 'Keefe, you are free to pick up your firearms in West Palm Beach at the Sheriff's Office." We won this round. But Patriot, the fight is far from over. The restraining order is still active. The legal battle continues. And the bills are mounting every single day. Pro hac vice attorneys. Emergency hearings. Court filings across multiple counties. This is exactly the kind of legal warfare designed to bleed a journalist dry until he stops investigating. "" Think about what's really happening here: a confirmed FBI informant who said he wanted me dead is using the court system to disarm me and silence my reporting. Our hidden camera caught Tyrmand admitting he served as an FBI informant working with the Southern District of New York -- against me. Instead of being held accountable, he filed a restraining order. Instead of facing justice for his threats, he's weaponizing the legal system to punish me for exposing him. This is what happens when you investigate the powerful. They don 't just fight back -- they try to destroy you. Patriot, here's what your donation funds right now: Covers court filing fees for one motion in this case one hour of legal research for James's defense Pays for pro hac vice attorney admission in a new jurisdiction Covers one day of emergency legal representation Funds a full court filing and brief preparation "" They took my firearms from my own newsroom, Patriot. Think about that. A journalist. In America. Disarmed by police -- because an FBI informant filed paperwork. If they can do this to me, they can do it to anyone. And if we don't fight back now -- with the best lawyers, in every courtroom, on every motion -- they will keep coming. I will never stop investigating. I will never stop exposing corruption. But I cannot do this without you standing beside me. "" "" In Truth, James O'Keefe Founder and CEO O'Keefe Media Group P.S. Last night they walked into my newsroom and took my guns. This morning a judge gave them back. But the man who admitted on hidden camera to being an FBI informant against me -- the man who said he wanted me dead -- is still using the courts to come after me. The legal bills are real. The threat is real. And I need your help today. "" Pop Acta Media | Republican Task Force PO Box 461 Fort Collins, CO 80522 |

Friend —
As public opinion in America has turned against Israel’s actions, there has been an effort by the pro-Israel lobby to paint Benjamin Netanyahu as the singular figure at fault.
The truth is, there isn’t just one man responsible for the decades of violence and occupation of Palestinian territories. It was never normal or acceptable, going all the way back to the Nakba in 1948 — the original campaign of mass violence and ethnic cleansing against Palestinians.
Yes, Netanyahu is a war criminal who should face justice for his crimes. But the entire Israeli government and military have maintained the occupation, maintained a legal apartheid, advanced illegal settlements, forced Palestinians off their land, imprisoned children indefinitely, and much more.
That’s not to mention the genocide in Gaza and the ethnic cleansing currently taking place in Lebanon, which polls show are supported by a vast majority of Israelis.
That’s why we have to stay focused on reshaping America’s entire relationship to Israel, not just Netanyahu. We are watching a society slip further and further into fascism, and unlike here in the US, there isn’t a big, popular movement that is working to correct course.

Maine State Auditor Matt Dunlap sympathized with the man who assassinated UnitedHealth CEO Brian Thompson during a campaign event this weekend, in response to a Democrat activist who lamented the paucity of would-be assassins willing to murder health insurance executives.
"With a lack of Luigi Mangiones, what are we going to do about the insurance companies?" the blood-thirsty Democrat activist asked.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c0775010-335b-4937-8bee-7af78c2a497b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
In video obtained by _The Robinson Report_ , Dunlap appears to chuckle at the mention of the leftist celebrity, who has been indicted on eleven New York State charges and four federal charges in relation to Thompson's shooting, including first-degree murder and terrorism.
This Substack is reader-supported. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..UwJlWqrK1r1rvZYrEzYoYUlK4_yVPAIRBESdqwx5Qu4?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=195681844)
Dunlap conceded that he doesn't think murdering people is "necessarily" the proper avenue for health insurance reform. However, he did empathize with Mangione, the 27-year-old child of wealth and privilege whom young leftists have taken as their spirit animal, much as an earlier generation took Dzhokhar A. Tsarnaev.
"Well, you know, obviously I don't think shooting people down the street is necessarily the answer, but you understand why people get to that point," said Dunlap.
Dunlap, who was the first Democratic candidate to declare his candidacy in the Democratic primary for Maine's Second Congressional District, has held a state job for almost two decades, meaning he's enjoyed the gold-plated health insurance that comes with working for the government.
He served fourteen years as Maine's Secretary of State, eight years in the Maine House, and is currently in his second term as the state's elected auditor.
Mangione stands accused of stalking and shooting Thompson in the back on a Midtown Manhattan sidewalk on Dec. 4, 2024, as the 50-year-old executive walked to his company's annual investor conference.
The words "delay," "deny," and "depose" were reportedly scrawled on the spent shell casings -- a riff on the well-worn left-wing slogan describing how insurance companies allegedly handle claims.
Mangione has pleaded not guilty. His state murder trial is currently scheduled to begin Sept. 8 in Manhattan. His federal trial was originally set to follow in October but has since been pushed into January 2027.
Federal prosecutors initially sought the death penalty. A Biden-appointed judge tossed the charge that would have allowed it.
Since the shooting, Mangione has become a folk hero in certain corners of the online left.
A GiveSendGo legal defense fund for him has raised more than $1.4 million. A warehouse arsonist in Los Angeles reportedly invoked his name in April after causing $600 million in damage.
Polling has consistently shown that voters under 30 and self-identified progressives view Mangione more favorably than they view the man he is accused of killing.
Dunlap is currently facing Jordan Wood, former Chief of Staff to U.S. Rep. Katie Porter (D-Calif.), and State Sen. Joe Baldacci (D-Penobscot).
The state auditor currently sits in second place in the limited public polling of the Democratic primary. A Pan Atlantic Omnibus survey released in March put Baldacci at 36 percent, Dunlap at 14 percent, and Wood at 12 percent, with 38 percent undecided. A University of New Hampshire poll the week before showed all three Democrats running essentially even with Republican former Gov. Paul LePage in hypothetical general-election matchups.
Whichever Democrat survives June 9 will be running in a district that voted for Trump by nine points eighteen months ago -- a district in which LePage has historically been popular and electorally dominant.

name: Sarah McBride
subject: You might have missed this news
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
In the face of this massive fundraising gap, I’m turning to you for your support.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3172%2E21716%2Eljz9pl)
You might have missed this news:
_“The Republican National Committee alone has about $100 million more than the Democratic National Committee.”_
Unless campaigns like ours make up the difference, that’s resources we won’t have to organize canvasses, train our volunteers, or run ads to reach voters.
**Elections should be about whose agendas and records will deliver the most for voters — but right now, they’re becoming about who can spend the most and shout the loudest.**
We don't need to match Republicans’ fundraising numbers, but we do need enough to run a strong campaign that can compete with the Republican noise.
I’ve had a target on my back since before I was first elected. And the GOP’s unholy alliance of right-wing billionaires, special interests, and Donald Trump will do anything to benefit themselves over working families — including trying to defeat me and our movement.
Unlike Republicans, I rely on grassroots donors — not right-wing billionaires — to run this campaign. **A single donor is allowed to give up to $3,500 each election, but my average donation online is just $35.90 — about one hundredth of a max-out contribution.**
I would rather be accountable to 100 hardworking people than to one billionaire. Because grassroots supporters have consistently shown up for me, I am able to remain focused on delivering for Delaware, fighting for working families, and holding this administration accountable.
[**In the face of this massive fundraising gap, I’m turning to you for your support. Can you donate any amount today to help us defend this seat and take back the House in November?**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20260427-1.I4uddD&refcode=em20260427-3172&amount=5&t=2&akid=3172%2E21716%2Eljz9pl)

Thank you for your support.

This is what it looks like when you're a threat.

Friend, Outside money just dropped into this race to run ads that attack Seth, and I think you deserve to know what's actually going on. **Independent fact-checkers proved that the content of their ads are misleading, based on a false characterization of a vote Seth took to condemn hate crimes. ** [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130282064/617232257/2090747700?refcode=260427_jp_eom5_img1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjUvMS83NDc1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0NGZmNGFhZS04NzQyLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Wey0UiKMtioLv4_U0L-Tw-SHIuHVKE69VJgEagIoVgQ=) The fact that our opponent has had to resort to such gimmicks makes one thing clear: Seth is a threat to the status quo. Seth is a threat because he's not only fighting for the things that really matter to regular people, he's actually fighting effectively and showing up for real people on the ground. Seth has real policy proposals, and he represents a new generation that actually understands how to meet the moment we're in with a plan. To the people who've been doing politics the old way for a long time, that’s a scary thing. The people writing the checks for this Super PAC care about protecting a system that works for them, even if it stopped working for everyone else a long time ago. They can't beat Seth on the merits, so they're spending money on lies. That should tell you everything. I'm not going to sugarcoat this for you. Outside money wins races when it goes unanswered, and our end-of-month deadline is coming up fast. The next few days are going to determine whether we have the resources to punch back or whether we let them drown us out. I've been doing this long enough to know the difference between a moment that matters and one that doesn't, and this one matters. **[Chip in $25 right now. Seth is a threat because he's not only fighting for the things that really matter to regular people, he's actually fighting effectively and showing up for real people on the ground. Seth has real policy proposals, and he represents a new generation that actually understands how to meet the moment we're in with a plan. To the people who've been doing politics the old way for a long time, that’s a scary thing. The people writing the checks for this Super PAC care about protecting a system that works for them, even if it stopped working for everyone else a long time ago. They can't beat Seth on the merits, so they're spending money on lies. That should tell you everything. I'm not going to sugarcoat this for you. Outside money wins races when it goes unanswered, and our end-of-month deadline is coming up fast. The next few days are going to determine whether we have the resources to punch back or whether we let them drown us out. Peter, If the name Calvin Duncan doesn't ring any bells for you, let me take you up to speed. This man just suffered one of the greatest American political injustices in recent memory.
Calvin escaped death row at Louisiana's Angola prison by being his own lawyer. He then ran to become the clerk of the New Orleans Criminal Court to reform the system that stole nearly 30 years of his life and won.
When he won, MAGA was so furious that an exonerated black man took control of this office that they introduced legislation to eliminate his office rather than let him get sworn in
But we just made history on the steps of the New Orleans criminal courthouse. Despite the protests and legislative efforts of our MAGA controlled State House, we swore in Calvin Duncan.
---

Calvin and I at his swearing in ceremony.
When I watched Calvin's swearing-in ceremony, I could see what is in store for Louisiana this election year.
We've had enough, and we are on the cusp of taking back our state. Take for instance the contest for Louisiana's US Senate seat, where Democrats have a once-in-a-generation chance to flip this seat.
Trump is trying to unseat incumbent GOP Senator Bill Cassidy and is tearing him apart by bankrolling his MAGA primary challenger, Julia Letlow. So while Cassidy and Letlow duke it out in the mud to see who can best kiss the king's... ring, Democrats in Louisiana are taking advantage of the chaos.
We are organized and ready to prove that Louisiana was never a lost cause--just a cause in need of some more champions. Calvin's one of those champions and I am too.
I'm the Democrat running for US Senate in Louisiana. I'm a row crop farmer from rural Tensas Parish farming the same land my great grandfather worked as a sharecropper but now I own the land I farm on. My message of economic populism competes with and defeats the fake populism of MAGA and when I am elected I will be Louisiana's first black statewide elected official since reconstruction.
We have always risen above the worst forms of oppression. I can feel the shift in energy as folks are ready to vote for democracy and reject this fascist oligarchy. Dear Patriot,
They charged a cop with a felony for stopping a riot. I am not making this up.
They want to lock him away for using **non-lethal bean bag rounds** against a violent mob that was blocking an interstate highway, hurling rocks at officers, and bringing Molotov cocktails to the party.
I have seen a lot in my years in law enforcement. I have seen politics poison the justice system. But what is being done to Officer Jeffrey Teng of Austin, Texas is one of the most shameless, stomach-turning betrayals of law enforcement I have ever witnessed.
** [It has to stop — and I need your help to stop it.](http://links.conservativesdefendingfreedom.com/u/click?_t=91d01aa68bbe4105984439520ca0f0af&_m=919c8c190e2b45f9a51e510e68df7bb8&_e=sU5Z2NRMB-2b58WFZVU_Fyplu8QKcmU_f0EwJayayMRW0SB_61XtH5AgBWcWYHe_6d8NampyntfkqsliDa7Ktzek5QzCKIVf7hzqS2qhtYUOVPFZYobajUrP6365L1n_bG819uSRvSdgc2g6M00erP5X27ztwnNU5YuFM01QNlUV00A1up7kG2LiPprNUb-1cCT0ILo6dB3We5OL6vF9b6_c4FkyxQX-MaBIT5Lkz32Nj9KRrLzzMAWHSJEUWW2d3r7cIgcWQsKhDUgCKdQohb346v4bJY0dOLd1gL3xkKb5o_ufqMS_4yLS9nJ1LoplSKDXdAFWmPUDwIpwvj4RmE8CCL2Dh3xhgv9ywsm5GxQs3EDwNWsqkfjZv6Lcxh8120PTN6JfRnK_oqAR6Rl3ebdItihLmbc5MdWyKi72082hGKGc6VjoMG1RgC5kV1wq) **

What started as a demonstration turned into three days of chaos: buildings looted, police vehicles set on fire, a rioter caught with a Molotov cocktail before he could throw it. It took nearly Austin's entire 2,100-officer police force to keep the city from total collapse.
On May 31st, a mob completely shut down I-35 — a major interstate highway — directly in front of police headquarters. Ambulances couldn't get through. Officers gave verbal orders to disperse. A police helicopter broadcast commands over a loudspeaker. The rioters refused.
**Officer Jeffrey Teng and his partner were ordered in to clear the highway.**
Officer Jeffrey Teng with his wife
When they arrived, the mob started throwing rocks. One of those rocks struck Officer Teng's partner square in the chest. Under attack, outnumbered, doing their jobs — Teng and his fellow officers deployed non-lethal rounds to stop the violence.
That's it. That's the "crime."
Now Jeffrey Teng, along with 4 other Austin police officers, faces felony charges. Meanwhile, District Attorney José Garza has dismissed nearly every charge against the actual rioters. The people who threw rocks, set cars on fire, and shut down a highway walk free. The officers who stopped them are being prosecuted.
This is a political vendetta by a DA who has made it his mission to destroy the men and women who keep order in our streets.
And Jeff Teng is paying the price. His career is on hold. His future is uncertain. His trial has been delayed again and again — meaning this family has been living under this cloud for _years_ with no end in sight.

name: Katie Porter
subject: Fuck Trump
body:
[1]LeftNet

Katie Porter spoke at the California Democratic Party Convention earlier
this year. Please take a moment to read her remarks below and [ https://act.leftnet.org/go/21583?c0=leftnet_em20260427_partner_ms_kp_em_leftnet.APXylf&refcode=em20260427-1609&t=1001&akid=1609%2E2118727%2E8CfMj9 ]then make
a donation to Katie’s campaign for governor.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

I’m Katie Porter. Some of you know me as the whiteboard lady who held CEOs
and billionaires accountable in Congress.

So today, I wanna start with one simple, powerful message we all agree on.

Say it with me. Ready, 1 ... 2 ... 3 ...

Fuck Trump.

Yeah, that’s right, Fuck Trump. Together, we’re going to kick Trump’s ass
in November and stop him in his tracks.

I’ll stand up to Trump and his cronies again and again, just as I did in
Congress — with or without my whiteboard. But this election for Governor
is about far more than defeating Trump.

We KNOW what Trump is willing to do and how far he’s willing to go — he’s
willing to kill people in the streets, to rip health care away, to
ruthlessly attack our democracy.

But this governor’s race asks US — what are WE willing to do? What is
CALIFORNIA willing to do for our democracy?

Who we elect as our next Governor is the biggest, most powerful statement
we can make in 2026 about who Democrats are, in California, and
nationally. About what we stand for, and about what we will do.

Let’s elect a bold leader who WILL DO big things – the things we have long
fought for. When I’m your governor, I will deliver:

* Single payer health care,
* Less expensive housing,
* Free child care for all,
* Zero tuition charges at our UCs and CSUs,
* And, thousands of dollars back in families pockets, by eliminating
California income tax for those earning less than $100,000.

Those are real affordability solutions!

For decades, we have fought for these ideas. We’ve organized. We’ve voted.
We’ve pushed this party to be better.

I am running for Governor because I am WILLING and READY to get those
things done!

But you know who is standing in our way? Billionaires and huge
corporations that have far too much power in our country — and too much
influence in Sacramento. I’ll take them DOWN and LIFT UP the working
people of this state.

Look I understand, there’s a lot that makes me unique in this race — and
some of that scares people. I’m the single mom of three kids, I push a
grocery cart, fill my minivan with gas, and pay the bills. I understand
what it’s like to watch expenses like utilities and insurance go up and
dollars not stretch far enough, because I’ve experienced that too.

We’ve never had a governor like that in California. Heck, we’ve never had
a governor in heels! And I think it’s about damn time.

My differences will make me a better Governor, better able to address the
challenges Californians face.

California Democrats, our country is counting on us to lead the way—to
send a message about our democracy — by rejecting billionaires and
corporate-backed candidates—and picking as governor, the ONLY candidate
who has NEVER taken a dime of corporate PAC money.

In this election, there is a very real possibility that Republicans could
sneak two candidates into the runoff. We CANNOT let that happen.

But let’s aim higher than stopping them. Let’s seize the opportunity to
elect someone who is WILLING to get big things done and READY to live up
to our progressive ideals.

My campaign IS our Democratic values, powered by small donations from
100,000 people just like you. And how you campaign is how you serve. I
humbly ask for your support, not to be Governor “Of” California, but to
govern FOR ALL Californians.

Thank you.

And Fuck Trump.

Katie Porter is running for governor to stand up to Trump and lower costs
for working families. We need your help to win. [ https://act.leftnet.org/go/21450?c0=leftnet_em20260427_partner_ms_kp_em_leftnet.tdL4g3&refcode=em20260427-1609&amount=5&t=1002&akid=1609%2E2118727%2E8CfMj9 ]Please make a
$5 donation to Katie's campaign today.

When I’m your governor, I will deliver: Single payer health care, Less expensive housing, Free child care for all, Zero tuition charges at our UCs and CSUs, * And, thousands of dollars back in families pockets, by eliminating California income tax for those earning less than $100,000. Those are real affordability solutions! For decades, we have fought for these ideas. We’ve organized. We’ve voted. We’ve pushed this party to be better. I am running for Governor because I am WILLING and READY to get those things done! But you know who is standing in our way? Billionaires and huge corporations that have far too much power in our country — and too much influence in Sacramento. I’ll take them DOWN and LIFT UP the working people of this state. Look I understand, there’s a lot that makes me unique in this race — and some of that scares people. I’m the single mom of three kids, I push a grocery cart, fill my minivan with gas, and pay the bills. I understand what it’s like to watch expenses like utilities and insurance go up and dollars not stretch far enough, because I’ve experienced that too. We’ve never had a governor like that in California. Heck, we’ve never had a governor in heels! And I think it’s about damn time. My differences will make me a better Governor, better able to address the challenges Californians face. California Democrats, our country is counting on us to lead the way—to send a message about our democracy — by rejecting billionaires and corporate-backed candidates—and picking as governor, the ONLY candidate who has NEVER taken a dime of corporate PAC money. In this election, there is a very real possibility that Republicans could sneak two candidates into the runoff. We CANNOT let that happen. But let’s aim higher than stopping them. Let’s seize the opportunity to elect someone who is WILLING to get big things done and READY to live up to our progressive ideals. My campaign IS our Democratic values, powered by small donations from 100,000 people just like you. And how you campaign is how you serve. I humbly ask for your support, not to be Governor “Of” California, but to govern FOR ALL Californians. Thank you. And Fuck Trump. Katie Porter is running for governor to stand up to Trump and lower costs for working families. We need your help to win. [ ]Please make a $5 donation to Katie's campaign today. AI data centers in the news
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260427-2760)
Peter,
Friend,
Two big news items recently broke on data centers. Here's what they mean.
We finally know the price tag: $2 billion. The Legislative Fiscal Bureau confirmed that Wisconsin's 2023 data center sales tax exemption will [cost us $1.5 billion in foregone revenue during construction](https://act.francescahong.com/go/11495?t=1&akid=2760%2E105371%2ECyctxT), plus $369 million every year after. That money could be funding schools, roads, and child care, but instead it’s going instead to Microsoft, Meta, and Vantage.
The same day, the Public Service Commission [unanimously ruled](https://act.francescahong.com/go/11496?t=2&akid=2760%2E105371%2ECyctxT) that Big Tech has to pay for the power plants running their own data centers. That's a meaningful protection, and it happened because thousands of Wisconsinites flooded the PSC with comments and refused to be quiet. The movement is working.
But we're not out of the woods. We Energies is still pushing a 9.2% rate hike over the next two years. New dirty energy is being built across this state — gas plants, generators — to power data centers, with the climate costs borne by all of us and the electricity going to none of us. That's why this race matters.
The most recent Marquette Law School Poll found 70% of Wisconsinites say data centers cost more than they're worth, and opposition has surged across party lines.
Even Tom Tiffany has jumped on the bandwagon, announcing this month that he'd end data center subsidies as governor. Yes, the same guy who's taken about $11,500 from the PAC tied to We Energies and voted to slash funding for the Citizens Utility Board, the ratepayer advocates who helped win Friday's ruling.
He didn't have a problem with corporate handouts before the polls moved. And let's be serious here: Once the cameras are off and his donors come calling, he'll change his mind right back. I've been leading on this issue since day one.
In January, I introduced [CONTROL-ALT-DELETE](https://act.francescahong.com/go/11497?t=3&akid=2760%2E105371%2ECyctxT), the most comprehensive AI data center policy plan in this race. I'm calling for a moratorium on new construction, an end to tax breaks for Big Tech, and public ownership of new energy infrastructure.
We have more AI policy in the works, and we'll be sharing later this week — watch this space for more!
